title: Run the Hardware Task
subtitle: Order the laptop and capture the confirmation
scenario: It is SD-1. The plan says the laptop must be delivered by tomorrow's start. This is a physical-world task the automation cannot finish itself - it orders, hands off to the people who ship it, and captures the confirmation. Record the handoff so the tracker knows hardware is really on the way.
input: Task: hardware for hire H-4021 (owner IT Provisioner, due SD-1). The role profile lists a Standard laptop. IT places the order and must capture a delivery confirmation showing it lands by the start date. Automation triggers and tracks; it cannot physically ship the box.
instructions: Record who placed the order (the owner of the hardware task).
Set the delivery target so the laptop lands in time for day one.
Confirm a delivery confirmation was captured.
Validate to mint the hardware handoff record.

fields.label: Ordered by
fields.explain: The IT Provisioner owns accounts and hardware; they place the laptop order, not Facilities or the vendor directly.

fields.label: Deliver by
fields.explain: The laptop must land by SD-1 so it is on the desk before the start date - delivering on SD or later misses day one.

fields.label: Confirmation captured
fields.explain: A physical handoff without a captured confirmation is a guess; the tracker needs proof the order is really on the way.

copilotPrompt: Capture a hardware handoff for onboarding: who ordered the laptop, the delivery target relative to the start date, and whether a delivery confirmation was captured. The laptop must arrive by SD-1.
successMessage: Hardware handed off. The laptop is ordered, tracked, and confirmed to land before day one.

intro.heading: Before you track: the physical boundary

sections.title: Automation has edges
sections.body: Some onboarding tasks end in the physical world. The workflow can trigger the order and track it, but a person and a shipping company put the laptop on the desk. Pretending otherwise is how a hire shows up to nothing.

sections.title: Trigger, track, confirm
sections.body: The automation's real job here is to place the order, follow it, and capture a confirmation. The captured confirmation is what turns 'I think it shipped' into a fact the tracker can trust.

sections.title: Timing is part of the task
sections.body: Delivering by SD-1 leaves a day of margin before the start. A laptop that lands on the start date itself is already late for someone's first morning.

sections.title: What you produce here
sections.body: A hardware handoff record - ordered by, deliver-by, confirmation - the task tracker reads as this branch's state. The medium tier backorders the laptop to teach the blocked state.

realWorld.soloRebuildPath: You'd place the laptop order, note the tracking number and expected date, and only mark it done once you had a shipping confirmation in hand.

tools.powerAutomate: create a procurement item, then wait for a shipping-confirmation email/flag
tools.zapier: 'Create Order' then capture the tracking number into the record
tools.python: call the asset-order API and store the returned tracking id

takeaway.heading: Hardware handed off
points: You captured who ordered the laptop and the delivery target (SD-1).
The delivery confirmation was captured, so the tracker trusts it is on the way.
The task is a handoff to the physical world - automation triggers and tracks, it does not ship.
Delivering by SD-1 leaves margin before the start date.
The workflow can now provision hardware and prove it, not just assume it.
